Method of Attack: Use of droppers (multi-stage infection process) to bypass Google Play Store security scans
Droppers request minimal permissions and delay malicious payload execution to evade detection
Droppers download and install more potent mobile banking trojans after initial installation
Downloader-as-a-Service (DaaS) model renting dropper install space to multiple malware groups
Malicious code activation triggered by commands from command-and-control servers or user activity
Attack Vector: Google Play Store apps disguised as legitimate applications
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious downloaders fetching banking trojans from criminal command-and-control (C&C) servers
Droppers with similar code panels reused across campaigns
Delayed execution and conditional activation of malicious payloads
